item.title: 🟠 New OpenSSH Vulnerability
item.description:
Why this matters: Could affect sign-ins, MFA, or Conditional Access — watch for authentication issues.

It’s a bad one, and it’s been in the code for a decade:

A newly disclosed flaw involving OpenSSH and musl, dubbed “*sshole,” allows attackers to log in to certain Alpine Linux and other musl-based Linux accounts configured to block password authentication simply by entering an oversized password.

“Oversized” means longer than 256 bytes. Details.

Slashdot thread. And another news article.



Source: Schneier on Security  |  Severity: Important  |  Age: 1d

item.title: 🟠 Scans for Sshole Vulnerability (CVE-2026-123158), (Sun, Nov 8th)
item.description:
Why this matters: Early technical signal — worth a quick scan for issues that may become more important.

Our honeypots use "Cowrie" to collect SSH data. With the emergence of the "sshole" vulnerability last week, we are now seeing an increase in attempts to exploit the vulnerability. Our data is a bit limited in this respect. Our honeypots collect only the first 255 characters of SSH passwords. Longer passwords are highly unusual and not used for the usual password brute-forcing we observe.

item.title: 🔵 Srsly Risky Biz: The ritual bitcoin sacrifices will continue until security improves
item.description:
Why this matters: Could affect email access or mail flow — monitor delivery and Outlook behavior.
Tom Uren and Amberleigh Jack talk about North Korea’s hack of the Binance cryptocurrency exchange. Binance’s founder CZ says it is a wake up call for real banks, but he’s wrong. Even though they are probably just as hackable as crypto exchanges, real banks cooperate to reverse fraudulent transactions and it is far harder to get away with billions. They also discuss the pressure being felt in tech firms everywhere to speed up software development using AI. From a security perspective, results will be mixed. This episode is also available on YouTube.

Source: Risky Business News  |  Severity: FYI  |  Age: 7d
